nodes.title: Authentication Middleware
nodes.description: Express middleware that extracts the Bearer token from the Authorization header, verifies it as an access token via JWT utilities, looks up the user in the database, and attaches the full Prisma User to `req.user`. Defines the `AuthedRequest` interface extending Express Request.

nodes.title: Error Handler Middleware
nodes.description: Global Express error middleware. `errorHandler` distinguishes `AppError` instances (returns status and message) from unhandled errors (returns 500 with logging). `notFound` returns a 404 JSON response for unmatched routes.

nodes.title: Rate Limiting & Login Lockout
nodes.description: Express rate limiters for different endpoints: `globalRateLimiter` (300 req/min), `authRateLimiter` (60 req/15 min), `loginRateLimiter` (10 req/15 min per IP+email), `registerRateLimiter` (20 req/hr). Also implements an in-memory login failure lockout mechanism with `assertNotLocked`, `recordLoginFailure`, and `resetLoginFailures` — locks an email for 30 minutes after 5 consecutive failed logins.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `express-rate-limit`; lockout state is in-memory Map (single-instance only).
nodes.name: rateLimit.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Role-Based Access Control Middleware
nodes.description: Trust-scoped authorization middleware. `loadTrustContext` extracts `trustId` from params/body/query, verifies the authenticated user is an active trust member, and populates `req.trustMember` and `req.effectivePermissions`. `requirePermission` gates access on specific permissions. `requireTrustAccess` is a stricter variant that requires the trustId parameter. Uses `permissionsForRole` from `@pavati/shared` for default role-permission mapping.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on `@pavati/shared` for `permissionsForRole` and `Permission` type.
nodes.name: rbac.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Zod Validation Middleware
nodes.description: Express middleware factories that validate request body, query, or path parameters against a Zod schema. On failure, returns a 422 AppError with flattened Zod error details. On success, replaces `req.body`/`req.query` with the parsed (and defaulted) data.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Zod's `safeParse` for non-throwing validation; overwrites request properties with coerced data.
nodes.name: validate.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Authentication API Routes

All write routes use rate limiters and validation schemas.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses bcryptjs for hashing, google-auth-library for OAuth2, and jsonwebtoken for reset tokens.

nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Payment Campaign API Routes
nodes.description: Express router for managing donation campaigns (PaymentCampaign) within a trust. Provides a public campaign lookup by slug, and trust-scoped CRUD with auto-generated slug (slugified name + random suffix), campaign toggle (active/inactive), and deletion. All protected routes require auth, trust context, and `campaign:view`/`campaign:manage` permissions. Audit-logged on every mutation.

nodes.title: Dashboard API Route
nodes.description: Single GET endpoint returning dashboard data scoped to a trust. For members without `donation:view` permission, returns a personal dashboard (own donations, pending count, announcements, campaigns). For authorized users, returns an admin dashboard with aggregated totals (total collected, donor count, cash/UPI breakdown, today's collections), pending donation count, member count, recent transactions, recent members, and active campaigns. Uses IST timezone calculations for today's start.
nodes.languageNotes: Hardcoded IST offset (+5.5h) for date grouping; runs many parallel Prisma queries via Promise.all.

nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Donation API Routes
nodes.description: Express router handling the full donation lifecycle. Provides: collector-initiated donation creation with payment splits (CASH/UPI/MIXED), automatic receipt generation on successful cash donations, paginated filtered listing with permission-based scoping (own-only vs all), single donation detail view, donation voiding (cancels donation and voids receipts), split verification flow (verifying all splits promotes a PENDING donation to SUCCEEDED and issues a receipt), and self-donation for online UPI payments. Includes WhatsApp share URL generation and receipt notification dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Complex Zod schema composition with inline query schema; references services/receipts and services/notifications.

nodes.title: Trust Member Management Routes

Provides: paginated member listing with search, adding members (auto-creates user accounts if needed, handles re-activation of removed members), updating member roles/permissions/positions, soft-removing members (with protections for PRIMARY_ADMIN and self-removal), invitation token generation with 7-day expiry, invitation acceptance with upsert, join-request listing and approve/reject workflow. All mutations are audit-logged.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses randomBytes for invitation tokens; handles multiple user-lookup strategies (userId, email, phone).

All require appropriate permissions (`report:view`, `audit:view`).

nodes.title: Receipt Template Routes
nodes.description: Express router for receipt template CRUD. Provides: list all templates, create a new template (auto-activated if first), get single template, update template fields, activate a template (deactivates all others via transaction), and delete a template (prevented if in use by existing receipts). All require `template:manage` permission and are audit-logged.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `$transaction` for atomic activation; prevents deletion of templates with dependent receipts.

Provides: trust creation (auto-generates uniqueCode and joinCode, creates creator as PRIMARY_ADMIN), public trust search by name/city, trust lookup by join code, trust detail view (with optional public committee and recent public donations based on trust settings), join flow (supports OPEN/APPROVAL/INVITE_ONLY modes with join-code validation), committee listing, trust deletion (PRIMARY_ADMIN only), and trust update. Public endpoints require no auth; protected ones use loadTrustContext.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `randomCode` and `publicUser` from shared/lib; multi-mode join logic (OPEN, APPROVAL, INVITE_ONLY).

nodes.title: Messaging Provider Abstractions
nodes.description: Defines the `MessageSender` interface and three implementations: `MockSmsProvider` (logs and returns success), `MockWhatsAppProvider` (constructs wa.me URL and returns it), and `ResendEmailProvider` (delegates to the email lib with HTML templating for receipt messages). Exports singleton instances `smsProvider`, `whatsappProvider`, and `emailProvider`. Returns `SendResult` with success flag and provider response ID.
nodes.languageNotes: Strategy pattern with interface; mock providers are placeholders for real SMS/WhatsApp API integrations.
nodes.name: messaging.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: File Storage Provider (Disk / R2)
nodes.description: Dual-mode file storage abstraction supporting local disk and Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible). Provides `r2Active` check, `saveBuffer`/`savePdf` for writing files (with R2 PutObject or disk write), `fileFromUrl` for reading files back (R2 GetObject or disk read), and `presignedGetUrl` for generating temporary R2 signed URLs. Handles URL-to-key resolution for both R2 public URLs and local upload paths. Throws AppError 404 for missing files.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @aws-sdk/client-s3 and @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner; lazy-initializes S3Client singleton.
nodes.name: storage.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Audit Logging Service
nodes.description: Simple service that persists audit log entries to the database via Prisma. Accepts an `AuditInput` with optional actorId, trustId, action (typed as `AuditAction` from shared), entityType, entityId, and metadata. Called by nearly every mutation route across the application for compliance and traceability.
nodes.languageNotes: Fire-and-forget async function; action type uses `AuditAction | string` for flexibility.
nodes.name: audit.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Notification Service
nodes.description: Service for building and dispatching receipt-related notifications. Exports `buildReceiptMessage` (formats a plain-text receipt summary with amount, number, and verification link), `buildWhatsAppUrl` (constructs wa.me link with Indian country code), `buildReceiptWhatsAppUrl` (conditional WhatsApp URL based on toggle), and `sendReceiptNotifications` (sends via configured channels — currently email only — and persists each attempt as a Notification record in the database).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `formatINR` and `NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL` from `@pavati/shared`; channel dispatch is extensible via channelSender map.
nodes.name: notifications.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.title: Receipt Generation Service
nodes.description: Core receipt generation and verification service. `generateReceipt` orchestrates the full flow: resolves the receipt template (by ID or active default), generates a sequential receipt number via `getNextReceiptNumber`, creates a verification token, fetches background/logo images from storage, generates a QR code, builds receipt data (including payment breakdown for MIXED mode), renders the PDF via `@pavati/receipt-engine`, stores it, and persists the Receipt record. `verifyReceiptData` looks up a receipt by its verification token and returns a sanitized view (hides donor name for ANONYMOUS donations). `generateQrPng` produces QR code buffers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `qrcode` library for QR PNG generation; `@pavati/receipt-engine/server` for PDF rendering; atomic receipt numbering via Prisma transaction.
nodes.name: receipts.ts
nodes.summary: No summary available

nodes.languageLesson: Composing permission arrays with spread of shared base sets (everyone, ops) is a common RBAC pattern that avoids duplication while keeping each role's full grant list explicit and auditable.

The 'as const' on the dict object preserves literal types for all translation values. This pattern works well for apps with a small, finite set of translations and no pluralization or interpolation needs.

nodes.title: Application Entry Point
nodes.summary: React application bootstrap that initializes QueryClient, restores locale from localStorage, fetches the current user session via /auth/me API endpoint, and renders the app tree (StrictMode > QueryClientProvider > RouterProvider) into the DOM root. Uses a one-shot render guard to prevent double rendering during async session restore.
nodes.description: The application's entry point that orchestrates startup sequence: (1) creates a React Query client with retry=1, no refetchOnWindowFocus, and 15s staleTime; (2) restores the user's locale choice from localStorage; (3) attempts to restore the authenticated session by calling GET /auth/me; (4) renders the React tree once session restore completes or fails. The render function uses a boolean guard to ensure single execution. The session restore pattern avoids a flash of unauthenticated content by fetching user data before first render. React Query is configured globally for all API data fetching across the app.

Global CSS imported from styles/index.css. The api module is a custom HTTP client (not axios/fetch directly). Zustand store accessed via getState() outside React component tree for session hydration.
nodes.languageLesson: This file shows the pre-render session hydration pattern: fetching auth state before createRoot().render() to prevent auth flicker. The one-shot render guard (let rendered = false) prevents the async .then() and .catch() both calling render() if the API call completes after the catch. React Query's QueryClient is created at module scope for singleton usage across the app.

tour.title: Project Root & Monorepo Structure
tour.description: Start at the root package.json to understand the monorepo layout. Pāvati Pustak is a Turborepo-based monorepo with three workspaces: apps/api (Express backend), apps/web (React SPA), and two internal packages (shared types and receipt engine). The root defines scripts for dev, build, and deploy across all packages.
tour.languageLesson: Monorepo tooling: Turborepo orchestrates builds across TypeScript workspaces. The root package.json uses workspaces + turbo.json to parallelize type-checking and builds. SQL lives in Prisma migrations; Prisma schema is the source of truth for the database.

tour.title: API Server Bootstrap
tour.description: The Express server entry point at apps/api/src/index.ts is the highest fan-out file in the codebase (19 outbound edges). It mounts all route modules (auth, trusts, donations, receipts, campaigns, members, templates, reports, etc.), applies middleware (CORS, rate limiting, error handling), and wires up providers (storage, messaging). This is the single orchestration point for the entire backend.
tour.languageLesson: Express server pattern: a single index.ts imports and mounts ~12 route modules plus middleware. Each module is a separate routes.ts file. The server uses http.ts as a thin Express wrapper and logger.ts for structured logging.

tour.title: Database Schema (18 Models)
tour.description: The Prisma schema defines the entire data model: Trust, User, Member, Donation, DonationSplit, Receipt, ReceiptTemplate, Campaign, Announcement, Notification, AuditLog, and more. Key relationships: a Trust has many Members and Donations; Donations have payment splits (cash/UPI); Receipts are generated per-donation with per-trust numbering. Six migration files show the schema evolution from init through QR codes, donation splits, and receipt uniqueness.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma schema syntax: @id @default(autoincrement()), relations via @relation(), enums for roles and statuses. Migrations are timestamped SQL files; the migration_lock.toml pins the database provider.

tour.title: Shared Package — Types, Schemas & Permissions
tour.description: The packages/shared workspace is imported by both the API and web app, making it the contract layer. It exports TypeScript types (User, Trust, Donation, Receipt, Campaign), Zod validation schemas for all API inputs, permission constants organized by role (trust_admin, member, treasurer, etc.), and utility constants (festival lists, payment modes). The permissions module defines RBAC as a flat permission set; schemas use Zod for runtime validation.
tour.languageLesson: Zod schemas: z.object({ name: z.string().min(1) }) for input validation. Permission model: flat permission strings like 'donation:create', 'trust:admin' checked by middleware. Shared package pattern: re-export everything from index.ts.

tour.title: API Middleware — Auth, RBAC & Validation
tour.description: Three middleware files form the security backbone. auth.ts extracts and verifies JWT tokens, attaching the user to the request. rbac.ts checks the user's role/permissions against required permission strings from the shared package. validate.ts applies Zod schemas to request bodies. rateLimit.ts provides request throttling. error.ts is the global error handler. These are imported by the server entry and used by every route module.
tour.languageLesson: Middleware chain pattern: Express middleware functions (req, res, next) are composed. Auth middleware decodes JWTs; RBAC middleware checks permission sets; validate middleware parses request bodies against Zod schemas and returns 400 on failure.

tour.title: API Route Modules
tour.description: The API is organized into 12 route modules under apps/api/src/modules/. Each module (auth, trusts, donations, receipts, campaigns, members, templates, reports, announcements, notifications, uploads, dashboard, users) is a single routes.ts file exporting an Express Router. The server entry mounts them at path prefixes like /api/auth, /api/trusts, /api/donations. The donations module has the most outbound dependencies, coordinating with the shared schemas and middleware.
tour.languageLesson: Express Router pattern: const router = Router(); router.post('/', authMiddleware, rbacMiddleware, validate(schema), handler); module.exports = router. Each module is self-contained with its own route handlers.

tour.title: API Services — Receipts, Audit & Notifications
tour.description: Services layer sits above routes. receipts.ts orchestrates PDF receipt generation by calling the receipt-engine package, persisting receipt records, and managing per-trust sequential numbering. audit.ts records all mutating actions to the AuditLog model. notifications.ts handles sending receipt notifications via WhatsApp/email channels. These services are called by route handlers and represent the business logic layer.
tour.languageLesson: Service pattern: services encapsulate business logic separate from HTTP concerns. The receipt service coordinates: validate input → call receipt-engine for PDF → save receipt record → trigger notification. Audit logging is cross-cutting, called after mutations.

tour.title: Receipt Engine — PDF Generation Package
tour.description: packages/receipt-engine is a standalone package for generating receipt PDFs. It uses canvas-based rendering (node-canvas) to draw receipt templates with dynamic fields (donor name, amount, date, trust info), supporting background images and custom field layouts. pdf.ts is the main generator; layout.ts handles field positioning with pixel-level precision; types.ts defines the receipt template data model. The web app also uses this package for live preview rendering.
tour.languageLesson: Canvas rendering: createCanvas() → ctx.fillText() for text, ctx.drawImage() for backgrounds. The receipt engine is isomorphic — same code runs server-side (PDF generation) and client-side (preview via HTML Canvas). TypeScript types define the contract between template editors and the renderer.

tour.title: Web SPA Entry & Router
tour.description: The React app boots at main.tsx, which sets up React 18 with StrictMode, renders the App component, and mounts to the DOM. The router (router.tsx) defines the full route tree with React Router v6: public routes (landing, donate, verify), auth routes (login, signup, forgot/reset password), and protected authenticated routes wrapped in the AppLayout. The layout component provides the sidebar navigation, trust switcher, and header.
tour.languageLesson: React SPA architecture: main.tsx → <App /> → <BrowserRouter> → <Routes>. Protected routes use an auth guard that checks session state. The layout component wraps authenticated pages with navigation. React Router v6 uses element={<Component />} syntax.

tour.title: Web API Client & Auth Store
tour.description: The API client (api.ts) is the second most connected file (fan-in 33, fan-out 11). It wraps fetch() calls to every API endpoint with automatic token injection, trust context headers, and response parsing. The auth store (stores/auth.ts) manages client-side session state (user, trust, tokens) using a simple pub/sub pattern. auth-actions.ts coordinates login/logout/signup flows by calling the API client and updating the store. Every feature page imports api.ts for data fetching.
tour.languageLesson: API client pattern: a centralized fetch wrapper that attaches Authorization headers, handles 401 redirects, and manages trust context. The auth store is a lightweight state manager — setSession() updates subscribers. No Redux/Zustand — custom pub/sub keeps the bundle small.

tour.title: Web Shared Components & Layout
tour.description: The UI component library (ui.tsx) provides Button, Card, Input, Select, Modal, Spinner, EmptyState, StatCard, PageHeader, and Pagination with branded maroon/cream theming. layout.tsx is the authenticated app shell: a permission-filtered sidebar navigation, trust switcher dropdown, responsive mobile menu, and header. utils.ts (highest fan-in at 36 dependents) provides shared helpers. Every feature page imports layout.tsx and ui.tsx.
tour.languageLesson: Component design: ui.tsx exports ~12 reusable primitives with Tailwind CSS classes. layout.tsx defines navItems filtered by user permissions. utils.ts contains formatters, class mergers (cn/clsx pattern), and helper functions. CSS lives in apps/web/src/styles/index.css.

tour.title: Donation Flow — End to End
tour.description: The donation flow spans the full stack. CreateDonationPage.tsx (admin) records offline donations with split payment methods, proof uploads, and QR-based UPI collection. DonationsPage.tsx lists all donations with search/filter. DonatePage.tsx and MemberDonatePage.tsx handle public/member donations via campaign links. On the API side, donations/routes.ts processes the request, and receipts.ts generates the PDF receipt. This is the core business flow of the application.
tour.languageLesson: Split payment model: a single donation can have multiple DonationSplit records (cash + UPI). Each split has its own verification status. The receipt is generated after all splits are recorded. QR codes are campaign-specific and show the trust's UPI ID.

tour.title: Receipt & Template System
tour.description: Receipts are PDF documents generated from customizable templates. ReceiptsPage.tsx lists receipts with send/download actions. ReceiptPreviewPage.tsx shows a live canvas preview. TemplateEditorPage.tsx provides a drag-and-drop editor for positioning text fields over a background image. ReceiptVerifyPage.tsx is a public page for verifying receipt authenticity. On the API, receipts/routes.ts handles CRUD and PDF generation by calling the receipt service.
tour.languageLesson: Template system: each Trust has ReceiptTemplates with positioned fields (x, y, width, height). The editor uses pointer events for drag/resize. The receipt engine renders the template with live data. Public verification uses a unique receipt URL.

tour.title: Deployment & Configuration
tour.description: The Procfile at root defines the Heroku deployment: web process runs the API server, and the buildpack handles Prisma migration + build. Six migration files show the schema evolution. The project uses Vite for the web build, TypeScript with project references, and environment-based configuration. The seed file (prisma/seed.ts) populates initial data using shared constants.
tour.languageLesson: Deployment pattern: Heroku Procfile runs 'node dist/index.js'. Prisma migrations run automatically via build script. Vite builds the SPA to static files served by the API. Config uses environment variables with typed defaults in config/index.ts.
